recordRow.js.lastSyncResult: Pulled via get_design_context + get_variable_defs on node 21:2 (Desktop-Default). Compared every returned value against the real code/CSS: colors, nav-size/body-size, ent-title-size/ent-sub-size (verified as the exact 1.05em/.92em of body-size the real CSS specifies), row padding/gaps, and default content all matched exactly. The detail-row label-width(110)+gap(16)=126 exactly reproduces the real CSS's padding-left:126px via a different (flex vs. absolute-position) technique. Zero undocumented drift found — the one known simplification (fixed 800px row width vs. the real 100%-relative width) was already documented pre-pull. No code change made, since none was warranted.
recordRow.js.propertyReferenceCoverage: All 4 variants now bound (fixed 2026-09-04 during Phase 5): the original Phase 3 build only wired componentPropertyReferences on the Desktop-Default variant's text nodes — Desktop-Hover/Mobile-Default/Mobile-Hover had their own separate, unbound text nodes, so setting a property's VALUE had no visible effect except on Desktop-Default. Found via the Mobile whole-page assembly showing stale default content despite correct property values on the instance. Fixed by binding the same property IDs on all 3 remaining variants' equivalent nodes.
recordRow.js.note: Supersedes the archived change's proof-of-loop flat frame (was node 2:6, 'Record Row — IT WAS RAINING') — deleted 2026-09-04 with owner confirmation, per design.md's risk note requiring explicit approval before removing it. entityTitle/entitySub are NOT exposed as recordRow-level properties (see entityBlock.js note) — override the nested entityBlock instance directly. On Theme page.

section.js.note: On Theme page. Composed from the new Section Header molecule (Core page, node 33:69), which nests the Hide/Show Toggle atom. Body is a placeholder frame — real body content (tables/paragraphs) assembles at the whole-page-assembly stage (Phase 5), not hardcoded into this component.

toolbar.note: No components/*.js counterpart — static, singular markup in index.html, per design.md's scope. Composed from the Dark Mode Toggle atom. Height/padding bound to bar-h/pad-x, background to bg, border to line.

hero.note: No components/*.js counterpart. Composed from paragraphBlock (bio), Scroll CTA, and Hero Photo instances. Mobile variant reorders photo above text, matching the real @media max-width:768px order:-1 rule.

footer.note: No components/*.js counterpart. Composed from footerLink instances (Privacy/Location/Copyright/Email). KNOWN TRADE-OFF: fixing Copyright's mobile-width wrapping (footerLink text set to FILL) made Location/Copyright wrap to 2 lines on Desktop too, even where there's room — the real CSS lets each item hug its own width via flex-wrap, which this FILL-based approach doesn't fully replicate. Documented, not further chased given diminishing returns.

desktop.reason: smallest viewport at which every desktop-scale clamp() token is simultaneously saturated to its max — verified by computation, not assumed

mobile.reason: standard modern phone width inside the real ≤768px breakpoint; token values corrected to their true clamp() value at exactly this width (some were previously each mobile clamp's max, which overstated real mobile sizes)

spacingStepper.action: SET_VARIABLE on space-sm (12:17) with an EXPRESSION (ADDITION/SUBTRACTION, +/-4) referencing the variable's own current value — real interactive math on a token, not a static demo. Researched first: standard Figma design files have no native slider/NUMBER component property (that's exclusive to Figma Sites, a different product) — this click+math stepper is the closest real native mechanism. A third-party 'VariableSlider' community plugin exists but isn't runnable through this connection.
